title: A member question left unanswered for 14 days leaves the Member questions count but stays a to-do on the bell
what: After 14 days with no reply a member question stops being open: the member's app shows it as closed and lets them ask a new one, and the waiting number on Member questions no longer counts it. The bell still keeps it as a thing to do and counts it until the alert is deleted at 30 days, because only a reply, the member taking it back or a removal marks it done. The owner sees one number on the bell and a smaller one on Member questions, and a member who asks again gives two bell to-dos.
expected: The bell and Member questions use the same rule, so a question that is no longer open leaves the bell's to-do list (or both keep it until it is answered).
how_often: every member question nobody answers within 14 days
fix_line: Mark the question's bell alert done when the question stops being open after 14 days, or keep it open everywhere

title: When a person already called asks again online, their old bell alerts come back next to the new one
what: When someone with an open enquiry joins online, asks on the gym's web page or is invited again by a friend, the server moves that enquiry's next call to today. The bell's done rule reads a next call moved back to today as a slip being put right, so it makes the earlier alerts about that person (already handled as called) wait again. The bell then shows two or three to-dos for one person and its number goes up by as many, and those handled lines drop out of History.
expected: A move of the next call made by the server itself only adds the one new alert; alerts already handled stay done.
how_often: every returning enquiry who had a later call day set
fix_line: Only reopen called alerts when a person at the gym moves the call back, not when the server does

title: The server notes an alert as sent in the summary even when no browser got that summary
what: When the daily or weekly summary is due, the server marks every waiting alert of the gym as sent in the summary before it looks at any browser. If the only browsers with alerts on belong to signed-out people, or to people who may not see that alert (a question meant for one trainer, with only the desk's browser on), nobody gets a summary, yet the record still says it went. The at-once path does note 'sent to nobody' in the same case, so the two records disagree.
expected: The record says 'sent in summary' only for alerts that at least one browser's summary carried, and 'sent to nobody' otherwise.
how_often: every summary where no browser can receive an alert
fix_line: Mark each alert after the summaries are built, by whether any browser's summary included it
